- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show gradual, upward trends that diverge from true outcomes, suggesting failure to capture sharp downward corrections or volatility spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., 89+), model tends to overshoot and continue upward, while true prices often correct sharply downward or plateau.
- Model underestimates volatility in late periods (last 10–15 days of 30d), particularly when true prices show sudden increases or erratic drops.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — forecasts remain flat or slowly increasing even when true prices exhibit strong mean-reverting behavior.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true price correction.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture sudden, sharp reversals or “jumps” in price, especially in the middle of the 30d window.
- When true prices show a strong downward trend after a peak, model continues to forecast upward, indicating poor sensitivity to recent negative momentum.
